subject: elephantnose fish
title: This Fish's Brain Burns 60% of Its Oxygen. Yours Uses 20%

scenes.text: Your brain is greedy. This fish's brain is three times greedier.
The elephantnose fish of Africa's muddy rivers has a brain that is 3.1 percent of its body weight. Yours is about 2.
And that brain burns roughly 60 percent of all the oxygen the fish takes in. Your brain uses about 20.
Why? It hunts in mud. It generates a weak electric field, and its trunk-like chin reads the distortions to find buried insects.
Sorting its own signal from the noise takes so much processing that its cerebellum ballooned into a gigantocerebellum.
Guinness lists it as the most energetic brain on Earth. A fish that thinks harder than you, per breath.

description:
The elephantnose fish has the most energetic brain known, using around 60 percent of the oxygen its body takes in.
Gnathonemus petersii, an African river fish, has a brain equal to 3.1 percent of its body mass (about 2 percent in humans). Göran Nilsson's 1996 measurements found the brain accounts for roughly 60 percent of the fish's oxygen consumption, compared with about 20 percent for a human brain; Guinness World Records lists it as the most energetic animal brain. The fish generates a weak electric field and uses the trunk-like protrusion below its mouth to detect buried invertebrates in muddy water, and the enlarged cerebellum processes those signals.
What is the smartest fish you've ever met?
first_comment: Its brain takes 60 percent of its oxygen; yours takes about 20. Which animal do you think is the most underrated thinker?
